jane_sales: Heads-up — Acme POC hits 413 when they POST the full convo bundle (attachments + base64) to our hosted inference endpoint. They said ~38MB payload. Any fast ideas?

omar_se: Can you paste the raw error they get?

jane_sales: Paste from customer: ```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 39823742
< HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
< Server: Microsoft-Azure-ApplicationGateway/v2
< X-Request-ID: acme-req-001
```

jane_sales: They are embedding binary attachments as base64 inside the JSON body (can't presign because of their compliance process).

lucy_infra: Azure App Gateway + some WAF configs and fronting proxies frequently cause these 413s. Also check any nginx/api-gateway between us and customers (client_max_body_size) — many setups silently block large JSON.

lucy_infra: Quick triage steps: reproduce with exact Content-Length locally, tail our ingress logs for the trace id, and check Console -> network traces for the request id. If the AGW denies it, it will never hit our runtime.

omar_se: If they can't presign, two product options: (1) route requests to Dedicated nodes or Private deployment (VPC/on‑prem) where we control TLS termination and proxy config, (2) change client to stream or chunk the upload. Both require coordination.

jane_sales: Customer asked about pricing — will Dedicated cost more for this use case or is it just a config change?

raj_platform: Dedicated/Private is a different offering — pricing is via reserved capacity + platform fee for Private. From a technical POV Dedicated can be configured to accept larger request bodies (you control the gateway) — it's not about per‑token pricing changing, but you'll need a commit/contract to provision capacity and to change the ingress proxy.

lucy_infra: Workarounds while we sort the commercial path:
- Ask them to gzip the JSON payload (Content-Encoding: gzip) — can cut size by ~70%. But beware: some proxies still inspect body and will reject based on compressed length header inconsistencies.
- Send attachments separately and include pointers (I know they said compliance restricts this — we can propose short-lived encrypted object store as a compromise).
- Split context: only POST recent window + precomputed embeddings or metadata pointers for older context.
- Try chunked transfer (Transfer-Encoding: chunked) — but AGW and some API gateways reject chunked in front of WAF.

lucy_infra: Example repro command we use to test ingress limits:```bash
curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @large_payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Look for 413 upstream in the verbose output.

omar_se: Short‑term assist offer: we can open a support window to pair with Acme's infra team and reproduce from their network. If it's AGW, we can show them the header evidence and it's usually solved by increasing the body limit or routing via a dedicated ingress.

jane_sales: OK I'm telling Acme: (a) try gzipping the request and retest, (b) check if they can change to multipart + short-lived upload if compliance allows, (c) I’ll escalate Dedicated/Private pricing options.

deploy-bot: Note: canary that updated nginx proxy came out 2 days ago — if your tenant is on that rollout check `nginx.client_max_body_size` in the Console overrides.

jane_sales: Perfect — setting up pairing with Acme infra now. Marking as high priority for this deal. Will follow up with a summary and their compliance constraints. :+1:
